summary_en: This paper presents a dual-mode ultrasound and photoacoustic tomography system that uses an ergodic relay and a single ultrasonic detector. A one-time object-independent calibration represents 6400 virtual transducer responses, allowing each optical or ultrasonic excitation to be encoded into one temporal waveform and reconstructed as a three-dimensional volume. The system provides complementary optical-absorption and acoustic-scattering contrast, supports longitudinal volumetric imaging at up to kilohertz rates, and is validated through in-vivo human-hand imaging. Its coded single-detector acquisition and direct acoustic-optical image formation make it a strong core addition.

summary_en: This work develops a freehand optical-ultrasound probe in which adhesive-imprinted anisotropic holographic diffusers shape fiber-delivered excitation light into eccentric photoacoustic ultrasound sources. The design permits dense cladding-to-cladding packing of 144 fibers, achieves an acoustic source pitch below the spatial Nyquist limit, removes grating-lobe artifacts, and fits an 18.5-mm-diameter endoluminal probe. The system demonstrates video-rate real-time imaging with improved depth and image quality in a realistic endobronchial phantom, making it directly relevant to the repository's acoustic-optics and optical-ultrasound scope.
